title: Learn how a product goes from idea to results
summary: Every product team moves through the same broad loop: understand the problem, choose a solution, build it, release it and learn from the results. Seeing the loop makes everything else make sense.

beginner: Learn the loop: discover the problem, define it, design a solution, plan the work, build, test, launch, then measure and learn. The phases in this site's plans follow it. Write one sentence on each.
Read about the Double Diamond and sketch it. Note that the first diamond is about the problem and the second about the solution.
Read how the discovery phase works in the GOV.UK Service Manual. Write down three things a team does and what it decides at the end.
Match each phase to the risk it reduces: value, usability, feasibility or viability.
Pick a product you use and write what each phase might have looked like, and where you can see evidence of it.
Skim the Scrum Guide. Note the events and who does what. Remember that teams adapt the loop, and that it is not a straight line.
Explain the whole loop out loud to someone in under three minutes, using your chosen product.

toolExamples.miro: Draw the loop as a board with the questions each phase answers.
toolExamples.notion: Write one page per phase with an example from a product you use.

definitionOfDone: A one-page diagram of the loop in your own words
You can explain the loop in three minutes
pitfalls: Believing the loop is a straight line, when teams often go back
Treating one framework as the only way
